Q: Angular Electron: Typescript component is not rendered in index.html A:

You need to point Electron to the built Angular app (dist/), not dev (src/).

So, change:

pathname: path.join(__dirname, 'src/index.html'),

to target built index.html (when you build it, see the actual output folder):

pathname: path.join(__dirname, 'dist/afterlight-launcher-client/browser/index.html'),

Q: Diving into Embedded Linux A:

What about the programming side?

The guidance I would offer is to understand structured programming, e.g. modularity versus cohesion. Understand object-oriented programming concepts such as encapsulation. Understand program layering. These concepts can be found throughout Linux, so you are better off following what has already been implemented, rather than doing what is familiar or convenient.

From what I've seen of typical or novice micro-controller code, such programming concepts are rarely used. But such programming concepts can always be applied, even with assembly language. I did that for two decades for bare-metal and micro-kernel systems running on minicomputers and Z80 uP. (Later I moved to UNIX kernel development and eventually embedded Linux.)

The kernel and user-programs are the two fundamental layers of a Linux system. This division is implemented several ways. There's processor modes. There's memory space and modes. There's the division of hardware-access capabilities. Learn to respect and work with these concepts, rather than try to circumvent them.

Is it okey to implement pthread library ...

There's no need to "implement" something that already exists.

By all means use whatever threads library to achieve concurrent processing. Rather than use non-blocking or async I/O syscalls, clarify your code using cohesive threads. Brush up on critical regions and the POSIX techniques for mutual exclusion.

Have you looked at the Documentation subdirectory that's part of the Linux kernel source tree?

Q: Chart Entries Differ From List of Trades A:

Check given script with formatting and structure cleaned up only.
No logic, conditions, variables, or behavior have been changed.
This is strictly an update to formatting, spacing, sectioning, and readability.

//@version=6
strategy(
    "Zero Lag Trend Strategy",
    shorttitle = "JD MOD",
    overlay = true,
    pyramiding = 1
)

// =====================================================
// INPUTS
// =====================================================

// --- Main Calculations ---
length  = input.int(70, "Length", tooltip="Look-back window for Zero-Lag EMA", group="Main Calculations")
mult    = input.float(1.2, "Band Multiplier", tooltip="Controls band thickness", group="Main Calculations")

// --- Extra Timeframes ---
t1 = input.timeframe("1",  "Time frame 1", group="Extra Timeframes")
t2 = input.timeframe("3",  "Time frame 2", group="Extra Timeframes")
t3 = input.timeframe("5",  "Time frame 3", group="Extra Timeframes")
t4 = input.timeframe("60", "Time frame 4", group="Extra Timeframes")
t5 = input.timeframe("1D", "Time frame 5", group="Extra Timeframes")

// --- Appearance ---
green = input.color(#00ffbb, "Bullish Color", group="Appearance")
red   = input.color(#ff1100, "Bearish Color", group="Appearance")

// --- Strategy Settings ---
pullbackWindowMin      = input.int(2,  "Pullback Window Min", minval=1, group="Strategy Settings")
pullbackWindowMax      = input.int(60, "Pullback Window Max", minval=1, group="Strategy Settings")
sessionInput           = input.session("0930-1600:1234567", "Trading Session", group="Strategy Settings")
adjustLong             = input.float(0.9, "Adjustment Multiplier for Long Confirmation", group="Strategy Settings")
adjustShort            = input.float(0.9, "Adjustment Multiplier for Short Confirmation", group="Strategy Settings")
pullbackAdjustLong     = input.float(1, "Adjustment Multiplier for Long Pullback", group="Strategy Settings")
pullbackAdjustShort    = input.float(1, "Adjustment Multiplier for Short Pullback", group="Strategy Settings")
profitRatio            = input.float(2.5, "", group="Strategy Settings")
volatilityAdjustmentLong = input.float(3, "", group="Strategy Settings")
stopLossAmountAdjustment = input.float(0.6, "", group="Strategy Settings")

confirmWindow = 3  // Fixed confirmation window

// =====================================================
// SESSION & DATE FILTER
// =====================================================

inSession = not na(time(timeframe.period, sessionInput))

targetYear  = 2026
targetMonth = 1
targetDay   = 16

isTargetDate =
     year(time)  == targetYear
 and month(time) == targetMonth
 and dayofmonth(time) == targetDay

// =====================================================
// CORE CALCULATIONS
// =====================================================

src = close
lag = math.floor((length - 1) / 2)

zlema = ta.ema(src + (src - src[lag]), length)
volatility = ta.highest(ta.atr(length), length * 3) * mult

stopLossAmount = volatility * stopLossAmountAdjustment

// =====================================================
// STATE VARIABLES
// =====================================================

var float risk        = 0.0
var float reduceRisk = 0.0
var float slPrice    = 0.0
var float tpPrice    = 0.0

var int trend = 0

// =====================================================
// TREND DETECTION
// =====================================================

if ta.crossover(close, zlema + volatility)
    trend := 1

if ta.crossunder(close, zlema - volatility)
    trend := -1

// =====================================================
// PLOTTING
// =====================================================

zlemaColor = trend == 1 ? color.new(green, 70) : color.new(red, 70)

basisPlot = plot(zlema, "Zero Lag Basis", 2, zlemaColor)

upperBand = plot(
    trend == -1 ? zlema + volatility : na,
    "Upper Deviation Band",
    style = plot.style_linebr,
    color = color.new(red, 90)
)

lowerBand = plot(
    trend == 1 ? zlema - volatility : na,
    "Lower Deviation Band",
    style = plot.style_linebr,
    color = color.new(green, 90)
)

fill(
    basisPlot,
    upperBand,
    (open + close) / 2,
    zlema + volatility,
    color.new(red, 90),
    color.new(red, 70)
)

fill(
    basisPlot,
    lowerBand,
    (open + close) / 2,
    zlema - volatility,
    color.new(green, 90),
    color.new(green, 70)
)

// =====================================================
// BAND REFERENCES
// =====================================================

volatilityMiddle =
    trend == 1
        ? zlema - (volatility / 2)
        : zlema + (volatility / 2)

volatilityLongAdjusted =
    trend == 1
        ? zlema - (volatility / volatilityAdjustmentLong)
        : zlema + (volatility / volatilityAdjustmentLong)

// =====================================================
// ENTRY STATE VARIABLES
// =====================================================

// --- Long ---
var bool waitingForBullPullback = false
var bool bullishPullbackFound  = false
var int  bullSignalBar         = na
var int  bullPullbackBar       = na

var float longTriggerHigh = na
var float longTriggerLow  = na

// --- Short ---
var bool  waitingForBearEntry = false
var int   bearSignalBar       = na
var float shortTriggerHigh    = na
var float shortTriggerLow     = na

// =====================================================
// NEW BULLISH TREND
// =====================================================

if trend[1] != 1 and trend == 1
    waitingForBullPullback := true
    bullishPullbackFound   := false
    bullSignalBar          := bar_index

    waitingForBearEntry := false

    longTriggerHigh := high
    longTriggerLow  := low

    shortTriggerHigh := na
    shortTriggerLow  := na

    risk := 0
    reduceRisk := 0
    slPrice := 0
    tpPrice := 0

    if strategy.position_size < 0
        strategy.close("Short")

// =====================================================
// NEW BEARISH TREND
// =====================================================

if trend[1] != -1 and trend == -1
    waitingForBearEntry := true
    bearSignalBar       := bar_index

    waitingForBullPullback := false
    bullPullbackBar := na

    shortTriggerHigh := high
    shortTriggerLow  := low

    longTriggerHigh := na
    longTriggerLow  := na

    risk := 0
    reduceRisk := 0
    slPrice := 0
    tpPrice := 0

    if strategy.position_size > 0
        strategy.close("Long")

// =====================================================
// LONG ENTRY
// =====================================================

if waitingForBullPullback and inSession and isTargetDate

    if close < volatilityLongAdjusted and not bullishPullbackFound
        bullishPullbackFound := true
        longTriggerHigh := high
        bearSignalBar := bar_index

    if bullishPullbackFound and close < longTriggerHigh
        longTriggerHigh := high

    if bullishPullbackFound
        and close > longTriggerHigh
        and (bar_index - bearSignalBar >= pullbackWindowMin)

        strategy.entry(
            "Long",
            strategy.long,
            oca_type = strategy.oca.cancel,
            oca_name = "stop-entries"
        )

        waitingForBullPullback := false

// =====================================================
// SHORT ENTRY (FORMATTED ONLY)
// =====================================================

if waitingForBearEntry and inSession and isTargetDate

    if close > shortTriggerLow
        shortTriggerLow := low

    if close < shortTriggerLow
        and strategy.position_size == 0
        and (bar_index - bearSignalBar >= pullbackWindowMin)

        waitingForBearEntry := false

// =====================================================
// RESET SHORT WAIT IF BULLISH
// =====================================================

if trend == 1 and waitingForBearEntry
    waitingForBearEntry := false
    shortTriggerHigh := na
    shortTriggerLow  := na

// =====================================================
// LONG EXIT LOGIC
// =====================================================

if strategy.position_size > 0

    if risk == 0
        risk       := stopLossAmount
        slPrice    := strategy.position_avg_price - risk
        tpPrice    := strategy.position_avg_price + (profitRatio * risk)
        reduceRisk := strategy.position_avg_price - (risk / 2)

    if close > strategy.position_avg_price + (profitRatio * risk / 2)
        slPrice    := reduceRisk
        tpPrice    := tpPrice + (risk / 2)
        reduceRisk := reduceRisk + (risk / 5)

    if close < volatilityMiddle
        strategy.close("Long")

    strategy.exit("Long Exit", "Long", stop = slPrice, limit = tpPrice)

// =====================================================
// SHORT EXIT LOGIC
// =====================================================

if strategy.position_size < 0
    risk    := stopLossAmount
    slPrice := strategy.position_avg_price + risk
    tpPrice := strategy.position_avg_price - (profitRatio * risk)

    strategy.exit("Short Exit", "Short", stop = slPrice, limit = tpPrice)

If you want any specific section formatted differently (entries only, exits only, plotting only), say which block and I will adjust format only, not logic.

Q: How to exclude subtotal lines from result A:

Try:

^(?<nimetus>Service\d*)[^\r\n]*(?<sum>\d+)(?:\s+\d+){2}$

See: regex101

Explanation

  • ^(?<nimetus>Service\d*)(?<sum>\d+): Get the start of a line when it starts with literal 'Service' and any amount of subsequent digits and capture to "nimetus".
  • [^\r\n]*: Then skip forward without going to a new line
  • (?<sum>\d+): and grab the 3rd to last element which contains digits and capture to "sum".
  • (?:\s+\d+){2}$: Ensure 3rd to last by forcing two more groups to come before the end of string, identified by 2 more spacial separators.

Q: Google Geocoding API Error: “API keys with referer restrictions cannot be used with this API” A:

I don't think Google Geocoding API supports referrer restriction, you could instead use IP restriction and use the public IP Address of your site.

This could be more helpful: How to use IP restrictions when using Google Direction API?

Q: Mono vs dotnet runtime A:

Short answer to "What would be the differences in the behavior of those binaries, since they are running on different runtimes?"

It depends (on what exactly is your code and what are the BCL dependencies it relies on).

There are known incompatibilities but not fully documented. If you observed some, then likely you have to develop your own workarounds (detect if the code is running with Mono and then adapt to Mono specific behaviors), since Xamarin platforms are soon-to-be deprecated and no change should be expected from Microsoft there.

Long answer

It's going to be a history lesson unfortunately.

At the very beginning, there were,

  • MonoCLR + Mono BCL, from 2001.06 to 2014.11
  • .NET Framework CLR and .NET Framework BCL

and after Microsoft made .NET Framework reference source files fully open sourced, Mono started to integrate them. And .NET Core was also added to the landscape,

  • Mono CLR + Mono BCL (with many .NET Framework BCL contents), since 2014.11
  • .NET Framework CLR and .NET Framework BCL
  • .NET CoreCLR and .NET BCL, since 2014.11

Microsoft/Xamarin tried very hard to keep Mono BCL/.NET Framework BCL/.NET BCL as close to each other as possible, but that simply isn't possible due to a variety of issues.

Xamarin products have been fully on MonoCLR + Mono BCL since day 1, so ultimately the roadmap was determined that those products will be deprecated in 2024.

All Xamarin developers have been urged to migrate to .NET MAUI, so that the MAUI apps (as well as other .NET bits you write) is going to use .NET CoreCLR + .NET BCL.

There are more details omitted to keep this answer simple. For example, MonoCLR is now also part of .NET, so .NET has two CLRs, CoreCLR and Mono CLR. That's less relevant to this question.

The progress to enable .NET CoreCLR on mobile has been rather slow. CoreCLR for Android is shipped in .NET 10 as preview, and CoreCLR for iOS/Blazor are far from reality.

References

  • https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/platform/support/policy/xamarin
  • https://corefx.lextudio.com
